answer: Resist sybils with latency-triangulated proof of location: each epoch, independent beacons send surprise timing challenges and measure round-trip delays, pinning every identity to one physical spot on the atlas, like a copper wire traced to a single ridge. One machine can only answer from one place, so a thousand clones collapse to one dot. A farmer must rent real machines in a thousand towns, each with its own power, rent, and upkeep — cloning stops being free and starts costing geography.
